llm.summary: This skill is a clearly documented self-hosted speech service integration, with meaningful privacy risks disclosed rather than hidden.

dimensions.detail: Outbound HTTP, model downloads, GPU use, and large disk requirements are proportionate for ASR/TTS, though operators should bind to localhost or require TLS and bearer auth for exposed deployments.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup relies on Docker images from the named project and a host-mounted data directory; the commands are explicit and not framed as automatic or hidden installation behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses user-invoked curl, ffmpeg, docker, and MCP setup commands, but it repeatedly warns that data is sent to the configured TALKIES_URL and that agents should avoid unmanaged file enumeration or deletion.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Server-side staged files, URL-download caches, custom voices, and model data persist under the configured data directory, but the artifact discloses this clearly and gives cleanup and access-control guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The network calls, transcription, TTS, voice-cloning examples, Docker setup, and optional MCP/file-staging workflows all align with the stated purpose of operating a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible speech service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the talkies server you point TALKIES_URL at. Use localhost or HTTPS with TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN for shared or remote deployments, avoid sending secrets or private media to untrusted servers, get explicit consent before voice cloning, and clean up staged files and cached URL downloads when finished.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The flagged TTS calls do transmit input text to TALKIES_URL, but that is the core function of this integration and the skill prominently warns that data leaves the host and should only be sent to a trusted server.
[E1] expected: The voice-cloning workflow can expose voice-reference material to the configured service, but the artifact repeatedly discloses consent requirements, trusted-server expectations, and custom voice storage behavior.
[E1] expected: Repeated speech synthesis examples use the same disclosed external-service pattern; I found no hidden destination, credential harvesting, or unrelated exfiltration behavior.
